title: Classroom CO2 Ventilation Balance Explorer
description: Calculate the steady-state carbon dioxide concentration in a room from the number of occupants and the outdoor airflow, to within 25 ppm, and the airflow needed to hold a target.
creator: The Science of the Built Environment
author: Dan McCreary
subject: The Science of the Built Environment
chapter_title: Appendix F: Smart Sensors and Building Automation

prerequisites: CO2 generation of a resting adult

pedagogical.learningObjective: Calculate the steady-state carbon dioxide concentration in a room from the number of occupants and the outdoor airflow, to within 25 ppm, and the airflow needed to hold a target.
recommendedUsage: Read the setting of challenge 1 and type the level where the carbon dioxide will settle, in ppm. Press Check.
After each answer the graph plays the concentration rising from 420 ppm and settling at the steady level.
In challenge 3, set the airflow slider to the smallest allowed airflow that holds 1,000 ppm. In challenge 4, decide whether the controller sees a problem.
When the controls unlock, change occupants, airflow, and sensor location and watch the steady level, the curve, and the sensor reading.
activities: Predict and calculate (10 min): For each challenge compute the answer by hand before pressing Check.
Halve the air (5 min): Reduce the airflow from 450 cfm to 250 cfm and record the steady level and the time to settle.
Where is the sensor? (10 min): Compare the three sensor locations at 300 cfm and explain which reading a controller should trust.
assessment: Students compute the steady level for 20 occupants at 400 cfm.
Students explain why a reading of 2,000 ppm means the ventilation is less than half of what was wanted.
